chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Let one of you adorn himself for his Muslim brother just as he adorns himself for the stranger whom he loves to see in the best appearance.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic etiquette for dressing and behaving when meeting a fellow Muslim?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam Ali (AS) elevates the act of grooming and dressing well from mere vanity to an act of respect (adab) towards one's brother in faith, reflecting the inner beauty of the soul. It underscores the Shia emphasis on outward presentation as a manifestation of inner dignity and social courtesy, ensuring that interactions among believers are marked by honor and aesthetic care.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Let one of you outfit for your Muslim brother just as he outfits himself for the stranger whom he loves that he should see him in a good state’.
en.sarwar: 10. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Qasim ibn Yahya from his grandfather, al-Hassan ibn Rashid from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu 5 minin has said, ‘You must dress up for your Muslim brother just as you dress up before a stranger; the Muslim brother who likes to see him (his Muslim brother) in the best dress . 555
